result.topic_en: Euler splits an infinite product 𝔄 into two partial products 𝔓 and 𝔔. He expresses each as a ratio of integrals following §17, rearranges them so that the condition ω−n>0 is not needed, and derives the successive coefficients 𝔅, ℭ, 𝔇, 𝔈 from 𝔄.
result.transcription:
190
atque ex §. 25. ad hunc casum generalem extense habebitur:
$𝔄 = \frac{(1-n-\omega)(1-n+\omega)}{1(1-2n)} \cdot \frac{(1+n-\omega)(1+n+\omega)}{1(1+2n)} \cdot \frac{(2-n-\omega)(2-n+\omega)}{2(2-2n)} \cdot \frac{(2+n-\omega)(2+n+\omega)}{2(2+2n)}$, etc.
$\frac{𝔅}{𝔄} = \frac{(n-\omega)(n+\omega)}{(1-n-\omega)(1-n+\omega)} \cdot \frac{1-n}{n}$; $\frac{ℭ}{𝔅} = \frac{(1-n-\omega)(1-n+\omega)}{(1+n-\omega)(1+n+\omega)} \cdot \frac{1+n}{1-n}$;
$\frac{𝔇}{ℭ} = \frac{(1+n-\omega)(1+n+\omega)}{(2-n-\omega)(2-n+\omega)} \cdot \frac{2-n}{1+n}$; $\frac{𝔈}{𝔇} = \frac{(2-n-\omega)(2-n+\omega)}{(2+n-\omega)(2+n+\omega)} \cdot \frac{2+n}{2-n}$;
etc.
Euoluamus valorem ipsius 𝔄 in duo producta:
$𝔓 = \frac{(1-n-\omega)(1-n+\omega)}{1(1-2n)} \cdot \frac{(2-n-\omega)(2-n+\omega)}{2(2-2n)} \cdot \frac{(3-n-\omega)(3-n+\omega)}{3(3-2n)}$, etc.
$𝔔 = \frac{(1+n-\omega)(1+n+\omega)}{1(1+2n)} \cdot \frac{(2+n-\omega)(2+n+\omega)}{2(2+2n)} \cdot \frac{(3+n-\omega)(3+n+\omega)}{3(3+2n)}$, etc.
Vt sit $𝔄 = 𝔓𝔔$, et vtriusque valorem per formulas integrales secundum praecepta §. 17 definiamus. Ac primo quidem pro infinito producto 𝔓 faciamus $a = 1-n-\omega$, $b = 1$, $c = -n+\omega$ et $d = 1$, eritque
$𝔓 = \frac{\int dx(1-x)^{-1-n+\omega}}{\int x^{-n-\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1-n+\omega}} = \frac{1}{\omega-n} \cdot \frac{1}{\int x^{-n-\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1-n+\omega}}$
siquidem sit $\omega - n > 0$. Pro altero producto infinito, sumendo tantum $n$ negatiue, fiet
$𝔔 = \frac{1}{\omega+n} \cdot \frac{1}{\int x^{n-\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega}}$
Ne autem conditione $\omega - n > 0$ opus sit, alia distributione vtamur, sitque
$𝔓 = \frac{(1+n+\omega)(1-n-\omega)}{1 \cdot 1} \cdot \frac{(2+n+\omega)(2-n-\omega)}{2 \cdot 2} \cdot \frac{(3+n+\omega)(3-n-\omega)}{3 \cdot 3}$, etc.
$𝔔 = \frac{(1+n-\omega)(1-n+\omega)}{(1-2n)(1+2n)} \cdot \frac{(2+n-\omega)(2-n+\omega)}{(2-2n)(2+2n)} \cdot \frac{(3+n-\omega)(3-n+\omega)}{(3-2n)(3+2n)}$, etc.
ac pro 𝔓 statuamus: $a = 1-n-\omega$, $b = 1$, $c = +n+\omega$, $d = 1$; pro 𝔔 vero: $a = 1+n-\omega$, $b = 1-2n$; $c = n+\omega$ et $d = 1$, eritque
𝔓 =

191
$𝔓 = \frac{\int dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega}}{\int x^{n+\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega}} = \frac{1}{n+\omega} \cdot \frac{1}{\int x^{n+\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega}}$,
$𝔔 = \frac{\int x^{-2n}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega}}{\int x^{n-\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega}}$.
Est vero in genere
$\int x^m dx(1-x)^{k-1} = \frac{m+k+1}{k} \int x^m dx(1-x)^k$,
ergo
$\int x^{n+\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega} = \frac{1+2n+2\omega}{n+\omega}$ [?] $\int y^{n+\omega}dy(1-y)^{n+\omega}$
$\int x^{-2n}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega} = \frac{(1-n+\omega)}{n+\omega} \int y^{-2n}dy(1-y)^{n+\omega}$
$\int x^{n-\omega}dx(1-x)^{-1+n+\omega} = \frac{(1+2n)}{n+\omega} \int y^{n-\omega}dy(1-y)^{n+\omega}$,
vnde concluditur:
$𝔄 = 𝔓𝔔 = \frac{(1-n+\omega)\int y^{n+\omega}dy(1-y)^{-2n}}{\int y^{n+\omega}dy(1-y)^{n-\omega} \cdot \int y^{n+\omega}dy(1-y)^{n+\omega}}$ [?],
vel
$𝔄 = \frac{\int y^{n+\omega-1}dy(1-y)^{-2n}}{\int y^{n+\omega-1}dy(1-y)^{n-\omega} \cdot \int y^{n+\omega-1}dy(1-y)^{n+\omega}}$ [?],
seu
$𝔄 = \frac{\int y^{n+\omega-1}dy(1-y)^{-2n}}{(n+\omega)\int y^{n+\omega-1}dy(1-y)^{n-\omega} \cdot \int y^{n+\omega-1}dy(1-y)^{n+\omega}}$.
Cum igitur sit
$𝔅 = \frac{1-n}{n} \cdot \frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(1-n)^2-\omega\omega} 𝔄$; $ℭ = \frac{1+n}{n} \cdot \frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(1+n)^2-\omega\omega} 𝔄$;
$𝔇 = \frac{2-n}{n} \cdot \frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(2-n)^2-\omega\omega} 𝔄$; $𝔈 = \frac{2+n}{n} \cdot \frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(2+n)^2-\omega\omega} 𝔄$; etc.
erit
